Lesson 7

Your ER Decision Checklist

Recall and apply the ER decision-making process when responding to conduct matters.

One Question To Remember

An employee may have broken a rule. What should I do next?

The ER decision process will help you answer that question fairly, consistently and confidently.

Your ER Decision Process

  1. 1Understand What HappenedWhat happened? What facts do I know? What information am I missing? Have I spoken to the employee?
  2. 2Identify The Rule Or DutyWhich workplace expectation, policy, rule or Common Law Duty may be involved?
  3. 3Apply The Fairness TestWas there a reasonable rule? Was the employee aware? Was it broken? Was it applied consistently? What response is appropriate?
  4. 4Decide The Appropriate ResponseIs a corrective conversation appropriate? Is a warning being considered? What outcome is reasonable and proportionate?
  5. 5Escalate When RequiredContact the Fuse when dismissal may be possible, a Final Written Warning may be required, a Shop Steward is involved, or you are uncertain.

What Will You Do Differently?

Your response is for personal reflection and will not be assessed.

Final Thought

Employee Relations is not about catching people out. It is about helping managers make fair, informed decisions when workplace conduct concerns arise.

Gather the facts. Follow the process. Apply fairness. Focus on improvement. Seek support when needed.
